one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 contains the Q3 2026 print: StockAnalysis lists Tue Oct 27, 2026 before the open as confirmed [3] (AJ Bell lists Oct 27, 08:30 [11], re-opened by the citation gate 2026-10-12; it no longer shows Oct 28; Corning IR confirms Oct 27); either way it falls inside the window. Guidance is core sales $4.9-5.0B and core EPS $0.85-0.89 [1]. Corrected base rate from the daily series [4]: release-day close-to-close moves were Oct 28, 2025 -3.3%, Jan 28, 2026 -5.0% (109.74 to 104.28; the +15.6% I cited in round 1 was Jan 27, the day before the release), Apr 28, 2026 -8.9%, Jul 28, 2026 -12.1% (143.36 to 126.01). All four were negative, but four observations are too few to tilt the centre, and the stock has already fallen about 39% from its June record close. The other events in the window are hyperscaler Q3 capex guides (late Oct) and possible ATM selling under the $2B program [9], a modest overhang. No directional call: lognormal centred on $156.68 with a one-month sigma of 0.19. The 20/40/60-day realized vol is 76%/68%/74% [4], and 0.72/3.5 = 0.206. I use slightly less because vol has been easing since July, but not much less because an earnings print falls in the window. Round 1 used 0.175; I raised it after recomputing realized vol. The post-horizon risk repricing in this revision changes 12-month value, not the one-month event distribution, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend of (1) 25.5x risk-adjusted NTM P/E on Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.13 = $130.8 (55%), (2) Springboard-implied NTM EPS $5.01 x 25.5x = $127.8 (25%), (3) a probability-weighted 10-year DCF at the horizon = $118.9 (20%); blended $127.7 -> $128. Core EPS already bears stock-based compensation (verified: no SBC add-back in the Q2 reconciliation).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.13 (SBC already expensed) x 25.5x = 27.5x peer-relative multiple less 7% for GLW-specific post-horizon risks (see long_dated_risks)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus core EPS. Corning's core EPS does not add back stock-based compensation: the Q2 2026 GAAP-to-core reconciliation [1] lists hedged exposures, translated-earnings contracts, debt translation, acquisition costs, tax items, restructuring, pension MTM, investment and asset-sale items, and no SBC line (Q2 SBC expense $135M, H1 $250M, is inside core). So SBC is already deducted from the EPS I capitalise; I do not also count SBC share issuance as dilution, which would double-count it.
Below FY27 consensus growth of +33% [2], because S&P expects hyperscaler capex to flatten in 2028 [8]. Operating leverage stays: the Q3 guide is EPS +28% on sales +16% [1].
$2.0B program [9] / $156.68 = 12.8M shares on 875M core diluted shares [1] = 1.46%.
0.25 x 4.37 + 0.75 x 5.38 = 5.13. Linear calendarisation, the same basis used for the peer NTM multiples. Round 1 used a geometric $5.17 with no dilution.

inputs_detail.input: NTM P/E multiple (peer-relative, before post-horizon risk)
inputs_detail.derivation: I rebuilt all 10 peers myself as Oct-9 close / calendarised consensus NTM EPS (see comps). Median 28.2x, range 16.8x-43.8x. I take 27.5x, slightly below the median, because GLW's next-year EPS growth (+33% [2]) is below the peer median of about +43%, and about half its sales are slower-growing non-optical segments [1]. On the same basis GLW itself is at 38.2x today (156.68 / (0.25x3.29 + 0.75x4.37) = 156.68/4.10). 27.5 x 5.13 = 141.1.

The GLW-specific probability-weighted effects in long_dated_risks are: fibre price normalisation -$6.0, expiry of the 2029 supply agreement -$2.7, further equity -$0.8, warrant -$0.15, hollow-core mix -$0.3. Total -$10.0 on a $141.1 base = -7.1%. 27.5 x 0.929 = 25.5x. The AI-capex slowdown risk (-$16.9 weighted) is common to all AI-hardware peers and is assumed already in the peer median, so it is not deducted again here; it does enter the DCF method and the bear scenario. 25.5 x 5.13 = 130.8.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Springboard cross-check: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) sales $26.0B x core net margin 17.1% / 888M shares = EPS $5.01 x 25.5x (risk-adjusted)

inputs_detail.derivation: Linear path between the $20B end-2026 and $30B end-2028 annualized run-rate targets [1]. The NTM window is centred on about Apr-2028, roughly 15-16 of the 24 months along: 20 + 10 x 0.6 to 0.65 = $26.0-26.5B. I take the low end because FY27 consensus revenue is $23.10B [2].
FY27 consensus implies 4.37 x 875M / 23,100M = 16.6% [1,2]. Add 0.5pt of further leverage (Q3 guide midpoint margin 0.87 x 875 / 4,950 = 15.4% [1], so margins are rising about 1pt a year) = 17.1%.
Same risk-adjusted multiple as method 1; 5.01 x 25.5 = 127.8.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Equity DCF at Oct-2027: cost of equity 10.3%; NTM EPS $5.13; 5-year EPS growth path 20.6% then fade to 3% by year 10; FCF conversion 80% rising to 95%; terminal growth 3%; that path values at $141.1 (the reverse-DCF of 27.5x). Then add the probability-weighted long-dated risks (-$26.8, including the AI-capex slowdown) and upside (+$4.6): 141.1 - 26.8 + 4.6 = $118.9.

inputs_detail.derivation: Conventional mid-range ERP. Cost of equity = 5.24 + 1.12 x 4.5 = 10.3%. At 9.5% the implied growth falls to 17.6%; at 11% it rises to 23.1%.

inputs_detail.value: 80% to year 5, rising to 95% by year 10
inputs_detail.derivation: TTM capex $1.52B is close to D&A $1.44B [3], but growth capex is accelerating (H1 capex $754M vs $516M [26]), so conversion stays below 100% while capacity is built and rises at maturity.

inputs_detail.value: 20.6%/yr for years 2-5, linear fade to 3% by year 10
inputs_detail.derivation: Solved so that the DCF equals 27.5 x 5.13 = $141.1 (reverse DCF). This is roughly the Springboard path to a $40B run-rate by end-2030 [1] plus continued growth after that.
Sum of value_effect_per_share in long_dated_risks: -16.9 - 6.0 - 2.7 - 0.8 - 0.15 - 0.3 + 4.6 = -22.25 net; 141.1 - 22.2 = 118.9.

bear.story: AI capex digestion as S&P's 2028 flattening [8] arrives early, while new fibre capacity (Prysmian doubling US output [25]; Chinese prices that had risen 80% [24] normalise) compresses optical pricing. FY28 EPS stalls near $4.4 and the market capitalises the post-2029 contract-renewal risk [26]: 4.4 x 19x (low end of the peer range: TEL 16.8x, CLS 20.6x) = $84. Precedents: $109 to $1.60 in 2000-02 [5], and -51% within a month in Jun-Jul 2026 [4].

base.story: Corning roughly hits the $20B end-2026 run-rate and stays on the $30B end-2028 path [1]; Oct-2027 NTM EPS about $5.13. The multiple de-rates from 38.2x to about 27x: above my 25.5x risk-adjusted value because markets rarely price post-horizon risks fully within a year, and below the 28.2x peer median. 5.13 x 27 = $139.

bull.story: Capex keeps surprising upward and fibre stays tight through 2028; FY28 EPS grows at the FY27 pace (+33% [2]), so NTM = $5.38. The market extends the Springboard path toward the $40B 2030 target [1] and GLW holds about 37x (today 38.2x; ANET/LITE about 44x): 5.38 x 37 = $199.

comps_summary.peer_range: Consistent-basis NTM P/E (Oct-9 close / calendarised consensus Oct-26 to Sep-27 EPS), 10 peers: 16.8x (TEL) to 43.8x (ANET), median 28.2x. Next-year EPS growth median about +43% (13% to 75%). Forward EV/EBITDA is not available at source for any peer, and trailing values are not comparable, so EV/EBITDA is left null.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 25.5x NTM (27.5x peer-relative less 7% for GLW-specific post-horizon risk), versus a 28.2x median (range 16.8x-43.8x). GLW trades at 38.2x on the same basis today (156.68 / 4.10).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. GLW's next-year EPS growth (+33% [2]) is below the peer median (about +43%), about half of Q2 core sales come from slower-growing Glass Innovations, Automotive, Solar and Life Sciences [1], and growth is partly equity-funded (the $2B ATM [9]). The small discount to the median reflects that growth gap. I dropped BDC and HUBB from round 1 because they have no AI-optical exposure (supervisor point, accepted). The supervisor's 27.5x appears to be the median of 13 names that still includes BDC and HUBB; the median of its own 11 kept peers is 28.1x, and of my 10 verified peers 28.2x. I still land at 27.5x, but on growth grounds, not as the median. SBC basis: GLW core EPS includes SBC [1]. StockAnalysis notes its peer EPS is non-GAAP, and several peers' adjusted EPS may exclude SBC; I have not verified each peer's definition. If all 10 excluded it, deducting their after-tax TTM SBC per share [29] would lift the peer median from 28.2x to 30.2x (an upper bound). Using the unadjusted 28.2x is therefore the conservative, GLW-consistent choice, and the unverified uplift is kept out of the numbers. Post-horizon risk then takes the applied multiple to 25.5x, still well inside the 16.8x-43.8x range.

thesis_break_reason: $100 is 19.5x my Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $5.13 and 22.9x FY27 consensus of $4.37 [2], below the cheapest AI-hardware peers (CLS 20.6x) and 13% below the Jul 28, 2026 intraday low of $114.50 [4]. Trading there would most likely mean 2027-28 EPS is being cut (a capex pause, fibre price roll-over, or a slip in the $20B/$30B Springboard path [1]) rather than ordinary noise at 70% realized vol. Lowered from $105 because fair value is now $128, and $105 sits within ordinary volatility of that value.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler capex into 2028, when the Oct-2027 price is set; S&P assumes flattening [8].
Speed of multiple convergence: GLW at 38.2x vs a 28.2x peer median on a consistent basis. Full convergence alone offsets a year of EPS growth.
Regime volatility: 68-77% realized vol and a 51% drawdown within one month in mid-2026 [4] make the 12-month outcome very wide.
Dilution and capital intensity: the $2B ATM [9] signals capacity spending ahead of internal cash.
The Springboard margin path is my extrapolation from consensus-implied and guided margins, not company guidance.
Peer multiples are themselves inflated by the AI cycle; if the whole group de-rates, a 27.5x anchor is too high.
Co-packaged optics could change fibre and connector content per AI port in either direction; I found no verified source quantifying the effect on Corning, so it is not in the numbers.
Cost of equity: the reverse DCF is sensitive to the 4.5% ERP judgment (implied growth 17.6%-23.1% across 9.5%-11%).
reasoning: Round 2 changes, all driven by the supervisor's verified findings, which I re-checked myself. (1) Multiple basis: the StockAnalysis 'forward P/E' I used in round 1 is price / current-FY EPS (for GLW 156.68/3.29 = 47.7x in the forecast table; LITE 50.65 = 1103.36/21.78). I rebuilt all 10 AI-hardware peers as Oct-9 close [22] / calendarised consensus NTM EPS from each forecast page [12-21] and reproduced the supervisor's per-name values exactly (APH 27.5, TEL 16.8, COHR 29.6, LITE 43.7, CIEN 39.3, FN 25.5, CRDO 28.1, CLS 20.6, VRT 28.3, ANET 43.8). Median 28.2x versus my round-1 29.5x. I chose 27.5x on growth grounds. (2) Base-rate fair-value leg removed: the supervisor could not reproduce the +6% conditional-return statistic, and the brief bars unverified claims from every number, so it is out of fair value and the ladder. (3) Earnings-day base rate corrected (all of the last four release days negative [4]); used only as context for the 1-month sigma. (4) TIKR claims (index reclassification, insider selling) and the thin Polymarket market are context only. (5) Post-horizon risks (method change 2026-10-12): the reverse DCF shows 27.5x needs about 20.6% EPS growth for five years after Oct-2027 at a 10.3% cost of equity, which is the Springboard success case. Weighting the GLW-specific long-dated risks (fibre price normalisation [24,25], 2029 contract expiry [26], equity and warrant dilution [9,26], hollow-core [27]) cuts the applied multiple to 25.5x. A probability-weighted DCF including the common AI-capex slowdown risk gives $118.9. (6) SBC check: core EPS already expenses SBC [1], so there is no deduction and no extra dilution. Peers' possible SBC exclusions would only raise the peer median (to at most 30.2x [29]); that is unverified and not used. Fair value is $128, versus $156.68 spot. Ladder: mixture of lognormals, bear 25% (median $84, sigma 0.50), base 50% ($139, 0.25), bull 25% ($199, 0.32). The resulting distribution has median about $140, mean about $148, P(>=157) = 0.376, and fat tails consistent with 70%+ realized vol and the documented 2000-02 and Jun-Jul 2026 drawdowns [4,5]. I centre between fair value and spot, not at fair value, because GLW's premium has persisted all year and Corning has $20B/$30B run-rate targets [1] to keep delivering against. Lane note: the 10 comps pages and the filings are out of lane by necessity, so the in-lane share is about 40%. In-lane work is the price-history base rates, event odds and capex-cycle context.

long_dated_risks.risk: Upside: growth above the reverse-DCF path (Springboard $40B end-2030 target beaten, capex keeps surprising)
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: EPS growth 5pt higher in years 2-5. Horizon value +$23.1 if it happens.

reverse_dcf_check: At a 10.3% cost of equity (10-year Treasury 5.24% [28] + beta 1.12 [3] x 4.5% ERP), a 27.5x NTM multiple on $5.13 ($141.1) requires EPS growth of about 20.6% a year for the five years after Oct-2027, fading to 3% by 2037, with FCF conversion rising from 80% to 95%. With a 17.1% core net margin and 888M shares, year-5 EPS of about $10.9 implies about $56B of sales around 2032. That is above the $40B end-2030 Springboard run-rate target [1] and needs roughly 19% growth in 2031-32 as well. It is plausible only if Springboard is fully met and AI-optical demand keeps compounding after 2030, which is a success case, not the mean, given S&P's 2028 capex flattening [8], new fibre capacity [24,25] and the 2029 contract expiry [26]. At 9.5% the required growth is 17.6%; at 11% it is 23.1%. The applied 25.5x requires about 19% growth at 10.3%, still demanding. That is why the probability-weighted DCF ($118.9) sits below it and the blended fair value is $128. Margins are held flat after 2028 because fibre price normalisation [24] is likely to offset further operating leverage.
